proposed.label: World Class Manufacturing
proposed.scope: Covers the World Class Manufacturing model, its technical and managerial pillars, Kaizen continuous improvement, and WCM tools such as cost deployment, KPI/KAI indicators and PDCA-based case applications; excludes reliability mathematics and scheduling algorithms.
proposed.source_sections: Chapter 1 Improving Operations Performance with World Class Manufacturing Technique: A Case in Automotive Industry

proposed.label: Overall Equipment Effectiveness
proposed.scope: Covers OEE fundamentals, its availability-performance-quality formulation, the six big losses, OEE variants (TEEP, PEE, OAE, OFE, OPE), data collection and automated OEE systems; excludes system-level design modeling covered under manufacturing system design.
proposed.source_sections: Chapter 2 Managing OEE to Optimize Factory Performance

proposed.label: Manufacturing System Design with OEE and OTE
proposed.scope: Covers using OEE and Overall Throughput Effectiveness to size production systems, external time losses, losses propagation between stations, buffer capacity and layout effects, and simulation of system performance; excludes single-machine OEE definitions.
proposed.source_sections: Chapter 3 Using Overall Equipment Effectiveness for Manufacturing System Design

proposed.label: Reliability and Maintainability
proposed.scope: Covers reliability basics, series-parallel and k-out-of-n configurations, hazard and time-dependent reliability models, repairable systems, substitution and minimal repair models, availability and optimal preventive replacement; excludes human reliability analysis.
proposed.source_sections: Chapter 4 Reliability and Maintainability in Operations Management

proposed.label: Job Shop Scheduling
proposed.scope: Covers the job shop scheduling problem, its representation via Gantt charts and disjunctive graphs, priority rules and performance measures such as makespan; excludes the specific metaheuristic algorithms listed separately.
proposed.source_sections: Chapter 5 Production Scheduling Approaches for Operations Management (sections 5.1-5.4)

proposed.label: Metaheuristics for Scheduling
proposed.scope: Covers population-based and local-search metaheuristics (GA, ACO, Bees Algorithm, EM, SA, Tabu Search, neural networks) applied to solving the job shop scheduling problem; excludes exact scheduling formulations.
proposed.source_sections: Chapter 5 Production Scheduling Approaches for Operations Management (section 5.5)

proposed.label: Just-In-Time Production
proposed.scope: Covers JIT philosophy, one-card and two-card kanban systems, heijunka leveling, JIT criticism, and alternative pull systems such as CONWIP, POLCA, Just in Sequence and Theory of Constraints; excludes the formal MMJIT optimization problem.
proposed.source_sections: Chapter 6 On Just-In-Time Production Leveling (sections 6.1-6.5)

proposed.label: Mixed-Model JIT Scheduling
proposed.scope: Covers the mixed-model just-in-time sequencing problem, Goal Chasing heuristics, criticism of MMJIT solution complexity, and simulation-based validation of JIT heuristics; excludes kanban mechanics.
proposed.source_sections: Chapter 6 On Just-In-Time Production Leveling (sections 6.6-6.9)

proposed.label: Enterprise Risk Management
proposed.scope: Covers corporate governance links to risk, risk classification, the risk management process (assessment, evaluation, treatment, review), internal control systems and business continuity management; excludes reliability engineering techniques.
proposed.source_sections: Chapter 7 Enterprise Risk Management to Drive Operations Performances

proposed.label: Packaging in Operations Management
proposed.scope: Covers the packaging system framework, its functions along the supply chain, consumer and company perception of packaging, sustainable operations links and mathematical packaging cost evaluation; excludes e-commerce channel specifics.
proposed.source_sections: Chapter 8 The Important Role of Packaging in Operations Management (sections 8.1-8.4)

proposed.label: Packaging and E-commerce Logistics
proposed.scope: Covers e-commerce's role in operations, packaging requirements for online retail versus physical shops, security and re-use of packages, and the wholesaler e-commerce logistics case study; excludes general packaging theory.
proposed.source_sections: Chapter 8 The Important Role of Packaging in Operations Management (sections 8.5-8.8)

proposed.label: Human Reliability Analysis
proposed.scope: Covers first-, second- and last-generation HRA methods, human error modeling in manufacturing, performance shaping factors, and the effect of rest breaks and fatigue on human reliability; excludes equipment reliability models.
proposed.source_sections: Chapter 9 An Overview of Human Reliability Analysis Techniques in Manufacturing Operations
